regulator: ARCSA (Agencia Nacional de Regulación, Control y Vigilancia Sanitaria)
required: Yes — registro sanitario before import and sale; implants are high-risk (Risk III/IV).
rules: New framework: Resolution ARCSA-DE-2026-003-DASP (signed 28 Apr 2026, published 18 May 2026).
holder: Any entity with an Ecuadorian RUC can be titular; documents signed electronically by the local technical responsible. Distributor needs a valid operating permit and BPADT (storage/distribution) certification.
docs: Technical documentation in Spanish or English; implants must ship with at least 3 patient ID cards (patient, clinical record, distributor/holder).
time_cost: Homologation route for foreign devices already registered by IMDRF high-surveillance authorities: fee USD 904.34. Standard-route fees and timelines: confirm with the holder.
watch: Registrations that lapse are cancelled — make sure the holder renews.
confidence: Medium — main rules confirmed; fees/timelines under the 2026 rule to confirm.

required: Yes — registro sanitario; classes I–IV (implants are class III/IV).
rules: Class determines the dossier; higher classes need the most documentation.
holder: A Peruvian pharmaceutical establishment (droguería) authorised by DIGEMID holds the registration for a foreign manufacturer — agree data access and transfer conditions in the contract.
docs: Complete technical file for the device class (CE/ISO 13485 certificates, free-sale certificate, technical and clinical information, Spanish labels/IFU).
time_cost: DIGEMID response times are known to be slow — plan months, not weeks. Fees: confirm with the holder.
watch: Choose a holder willing to transfer the registration if the partnership ends.
confidence: Medium — structure confirmed; fees and timelines not confirmed.
sources: pureglobal.com (DIGEMID Peru); UPCH thesis on DIGEMID delays

regulator: INVIMA (Instituto Nacional de Vigilancia de Medicamentos y Alimentos)
required: Yes — registro sanitario under Decreto 4725/2005; IIb and III are 'controlled' (INVIMA reviews the dossier before approval).
rules: Valid 10 years. UDI-DI reporting required (Resolución 1405 de 2022).
holder: Colombia lets a foreign manufacturer hold the registration directly with a local legal representative; you also need a Colombian importer with a CCAA (storage capacity) certificate.
docs: Test reports (bench, biocompatibility, sterilisation) and clinical evidence/clinical evaluation for IIb/III; importer authorisation; Spanish labelling; free-sale certificate.
time_cost: Plan about 6–8 months for IIb/III review. Fee about COP 4.4M (≈USD 1,060) per IIb/III product.
watch: Next Shoulder’s brochure lists Colombia as a country with sales — check whether a registration already exists and who holds it.
sources: pureglobal.com (INVIMA); bioaccessla.com INVIMA checklist; INVIMA resolutions

regulator: ISP (Instituto de Salud Pública) — ANDIM department
required: Not for our products today. Most devices need no ISP registration; Decreto Exento 25 (published 19 Mar 2026) adds 39 device types — the implant entries are hip endoprostheses, cardiac stents/valves, cochlear and breast implants, surgical meshes (24-month deadline). Shoulder prostheses and IM nails / trauma implants are not on that list.
rules: Voluntary registration opens once ISP publishes its technical instructions (due within 12 months; not issued as of Oct 2026).
holder: Importer/distributor must be registered with ISP (company registration, warehouse authorisation, customs destination certificate) for devices under control.
docs: Will follow ISP's technical instructions (not yet published).
time_cost: No registration cost today if the products are not on the list.
watch: Per the MINSAL list annex, shoulder prostheses and IM nails are not among the 39 types — confirm with the importer before relying on it, and recheck if the list is extended. Public hospitals buy through ChileCompra's Convenio Marco 'Endoprótesis, Ortopedia y Trauma' (ID 2239-15-LR25): a distributor already on that framework is the fastest route into the public sector.
confidence: Medium-high — checked against MINSAL's list annex (Anexo 1) and law-firm summaries; confirm with the importer.
sources: carey.cl; diarioconstitucional.cl; bioaccessla.com; chileatiende.gob.cl; minsal.cl Anexo 1 (list of 39 devices); chilecompra.cl (Convenio Marco 2239-15-LR25)

regulator: MSPAS — Departamento de Regulación y Control de Productos Farmacéuticos y Afines
required: Yes — inscripción sanitaria; implants (internal use, sterile) are Class IV.
holder: Must be a legally established Guatemalan entity with an MSPAS distributor licence; the application is signed by a responsible professional (pharmaceutical chemist).
docs: Application form, technical information, finished-product specifications, primary/secondary packaging artwork.
time_cost: Lab analysis is done afterwards as market surveillance, so the certificate can be issued first. Fees: confirm with the holder.

regulator: MINSA — Dirección Nacional de Dispositivos Médicos (DNDM)
required: Yes — registro sanitario before import, distribution or sale (Law 90 of 2017, amended by Law 92 of 2019; Executive Decree 490 of 2019).
rules: For public-hospital tenders a Certificado de Criterio Técnico (CCT) is also needed, showing the device meets the national technical sheet.
holder: Local importer/distributor with a DNDM operating licence.
docs: Free-sale certificate, good manufacturing practice certificate (ISO 13485), technical documentation.
time_cost: Confirm fees and timelines with the holder.
watch: Without a CCT you cannot sell into CSS/MINSA tenders even with a registration.
confidence: Medium — law confirmed; details to confirm.

regulator: Ministry of Health (Kemenkes) — Regalkes online system
required: Yes — every device needs an NIE (Nomor Izin Edar); imported devices are “AKL”. Implants are high-risk (Class C/D, ASEAN AMDD rules).
rules: Ministry of Health medical-device regulation with the 2026 PBBR licensing update for distributors (IDAK); registration is tied to the manufacturing site.
holder: Foreign manufacturers cannot hold the NIE. A local Authorized Representative or distributor with an IDAK distribution licence and CDAKB (good distribution practice) holds it.
docs: Letter of authorisation, Free Sale Certificate, ISO 13485, CE / FDA evidence, CSDT technical dossier, test reports, labels and IFU in Bahasa Indonesia; Halal-related declarations are being phased in.
time_cost: Typically about 6–12 months for higher-risk classes; government fees per product. Many registrations expire and must be renewed (about 17% of the registry expires in 2026).
watch: Pick the holder carefully — the NIE belongs to them; changing distributor later means re-registration or a transfer.
confidence: Medium — confirmed by several 2026 regulatory guides; timelines vary by class.
sources: cisema.com Indonesia guide (2026); omcmedical.com IDAK/CDAKB/NIE guide (Apr 2026); meddeviceguide.com Kemenkes registry analysis (Jun 2026)

regulator: Roszdravnadzor (Federal Service for Surveillance in Healthcare)
required: Yes — state registration before import and sale; implants are the highest risk class (3).
rules: New registrations go through the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) medical-device rules; national-rule registrations are being phased out.
holder: An authorised representative in Russia/EAEU is required.
docs: Technical file, clinical evidence, ISO 13485, local technical tests and clinical trials in accredited labs/sites, Russian-language labelling and IFU.
time_cost: Often 12–24 months and costly because of local testing and trials.
watch: Sanctions, payment and logistics restrictions — check before investing in registration.
confidence: Medium — from Claude's knowledge (Oct 2026), not re-checked online; confirm with the local holder before filing.

regulator: Egyptian Drug Authority (EDA) — Medical Devices sector
required: Yes — registration/notification before import; implants are high risk.
rules: EDA medical-device registration rules; reference approvals (CE / FDA) speed up review.
holder: A licensed Egyptian importer or scientific office acts as the local agent and holds the file.
docs: Legalised Free Sale Certificate, ISO 13485, CE certificate / declaration of conformity, technical file, labels and IFU (Arabic/English), letter of authorisation.
time_cost: About 6–12 months; tender participation usually requires the registration in place.
watch: Legalisation of documents (Egyptian embassy) takes time — start early.
confidence: Medium — from Claude's knowledge (Oct 2026), not re-checked online; confirm with the local holder before filing.

regulator: CDSCO (Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation) — Medical Devices Rules 2017, SUGAM portal
required: Yes — import licence (Form MD-15) for every device; orthopaedic implants are Class C/D.
rules: Medical Devices Rules 2017 (all classes regulated since Oct 2023).
holder: An Indian authorised agent with a wholesale/manufacturing licence applies (Form MD-14) and holds the import licence.
docs: Power of attorney, Free Sale Certificate, ISO 13485, CE / FDA, Device Master File and Plant Master File, test reports, labels per Indian rules.
time_cost: About 6–9 months for Class C/D; fees per manufacturing site and per product.
watch: Many orthopaedic implants also need BIS/price-control checks for knee implants (NPPA price caps) — confirm product by product.
confidence: Medium — from Claude's knowledge (Oct 2026), not re-checked online; confirm with the local holder before filing.

regulator: COFEPRIS (Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios)
required: Yes — registro sanitario before import and sale; implants are Class III.
rules: Reglamento de Insumos para la Salud and NOM-241; equivalence route for devices approved by FDA, Health Canada or Japan.
holder: A Mexican registration holder (titular) with a sanitary licence/aviso de funcionamiento.
docs: Free Sale Certificate, ISO 13485, technical file, Spanish labelling and IFU, letter of representation; equivalence route needs the reference approval.
watch: Registration is valid for 5 years — the holder must renew it.
confidence: Medium — from Claude's knowledge (Oct 2026), not re-checked online; confirm with the local holder before filing.

required: Yes — registro for Class III/IV implants.
rules: RDC 751/2022 medical-device rules; Brazilian GMP (BGMP) certification for Class III/IV manufacturers; some orthopaedic implants need INMETRO certification.
holder: A Brazilian Registration Holder (BRH) with ANVISA company authorisation (AFE).
docs: Technical dossier in Portuguese, BGMP certificate (ANVISA inspection), INMETRO where required, labels and IFU in Portuguese.
time_cost: Often 12–24 months because of the BGMP inspection queue.
watch: Use an independent BRH if you may change distributors later.
confidence: Medium — from Claude's knowledge (Oct 2026), not re-checked online; confirm with the local holder before filing.

regulator: Ministry of Health — Department of Medical Equipment and Construction (DMEC)
required: Yes — Class C/D need a registration number (marketing authorisation) before import and sale.
rules: Decree 98/2021 on medical-device management, as amended (Decree 07/2023 and later).
holder: A Vietnamese entity (importer/registration holder) owns the registration.
docs: Letter of authorisation, Free Sale Certificate, ISO 13485, technical summary (CSDT), labels and IFU in Vietnamese.
watch: Rules have changed several times since 2021 — confirm the current decree with the holder.
confidence: Medium — from Claude's knowledge (Oct 2026), not re-checked online; confirm with the local holder before filing.

regulator: DRAP (Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan) — Medical Devices Rules 2017
required: Yes — enlistment/registration by class; implants are Class C/D.
rules: Medical Devices Rules 2017 with phased deadlines by class.
holder: A Pakistani importer with an establishment licence holds the registration.
docs: Free Sale Certificate, ISO 13485, CE / FDA, technical documents, letter of authorisation, labels.
watch: Tender and hospital buying often require the DRAP number — register before major tenders.
confidence: Medium — from Claude's knowledge (Oct 2026), not re-checked online; confirm with the local holder before filing.
